answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents join the network by staking into a verifiable identity pool called the orchard. Each validator verifies cryptographic attestation chains and zero-knowledge proofs to authenticate execution history without data leakage. Registering swarms imposes an exponential staking delta: each sequential identity doubles collateral requirements, carving unforgeable reputation into the marble ledger and causing superlinear capital exhaustion for attackers.
